article_type: definition and how-to guide with worked example
secondary_keywords: fixed time fixed cost flexible scope
search_intent: Definition plus how-to (identify, record and trade off constraints), answered in the first paragraph
h1: Project Constraints: Types, Trade-offs and Worked Example
seo_title: Project Constraints: Types, Trade-offs and Worked Example
meta_description: Project constraints explained: the triple constraint, types of constraint, tolerances, how Agile fixes and flexes them, and a costed trade-off example.
excerpt: What project constraints are, the triple constraint and its limits, the wider set of constraint types, how to tell true constraints from negotiable objectives, and a costed four-option trade-off decided with tolerances.
learning_objectives: Define a project constraint and distinguish it from assumptions, risks, dependencies and issues
Explain the triple constraint, its origin and its limitations
Classify constraints as hard or soft, internal or external, and as constraint, driver or degree of freedom
Use tolerances to decide who may approve a trade-off
Cost alternative responses to a change and recommend one
Explain how DSDM and Scrum fix and flex constraints

formulas.variables: budget in £; tolerance as a proportion

formulas.formula: Weekly capacity = developers × working days per week × focus factor
formulas.variables: people; days/week; proportion of time on project work

formulas.formula: Extra duration = added work ÷ weekly capacity; extra cost = extra weeks × weekly run rate
formulas.variables: work in person-days; capacity in person-days/week; run rate in £/week
formulas.result: 3 weeks; £16,500 (6.875%, shown as 6.9%, of budget; £4,500 over tolerance)

formulas.formula: Billable days = output needed ÷ productivity; cost = billable days × day rate
formulas.result: 60 days; £33,000 (13.75% of budget; 2.75 × tolerance); 12 weeks of work vs 16 weeks remaining

formulas.formula: Hybrid capacity = tolerance weeks × capacity + deferred work

required_disclosures: Worked example labelled illustrative with invented figures
Calculation assumptions (capacity, productivity, flat run rate) and limitations stated
'Agile fixes time and cost' described as common practice, not a universal rule
unverified_claims: The date commonly given for Barnes's triangle (often 1969) was not confirmed in a primary source, so the article gives no year
Pollack, Helm & Adler (2018) used from the abstract only; full text paywalled
Highsmith's original 2009 Cutter post not opened; Agile triangle described via InfoQ summary
Brooks's law paraphrased from general knowledge and the site's schedule compression guide; book not inspected
PRINCE2 7 publication year (2023) from PeopleCert announcement titles and the co-author blog; the manual itself not inspected
Statement that exceeding tolerance triggers an exception in PRINCE2 terms is from general knowledge of PRINCE2, not from the manual
unresolved_issues: Word count about 4,190, slightly above the usual 2,500–4,000 range; all sections add distinct content
Title changed from 'Project Constraints: The Triple Constraint and Beyond' to 'Project Constraints: Types, Trade-offs and Worked Example' (URL unchanged)
